q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Net sales did not fall vs the previous day — measured net sales were ₹91,220 on 2026-10-13, up from ₹42,177 on 2026-10-12; however 2026-10-13 was about 12.0% below the modelled "usual" level (₹103,273). Measured.

Evidence
- Measured: Net sales — 2026-10-12: ₹42,177 → 2026-10-13: ₹91,220 (yesterday).  
- Measured: Versus the usual baseline for that weekday — usual: ₹103,273 → yesterday: ₹91,220 (−12.0%).  
- Measured (top contributors to the difference vs the usual baseline):  
  - Gross sales effect: −₹8,594 (71% of the Net sales change).  
  - Return revenue effect: −₹15,852 (132% of the Net sales change).  
  - Net-sales deductions rose: effect −₹1,635 (14% of the change).  
  - P&L ad spend fell (contribution margin effect): −₹14,762 (122% of the change).  
- Measured (campaign-level mover): ad name TH-471-PLAYSCRATCHLOUNGE_IMG_6516 moved from ₹0 → ₹24,962 and shows up as a top mover vs the usual baseline (≈207% of the change).  
- Measured (other levers): Orders rose 26 → 45 (+73%); conversion rate 0.46% → 1.11% (+140%); ad spend ₹38,661 → ₹50,408 (+30%). These moved with the day but the diagnostic found no supported causal driver.

Interpretation (short)
- The user's premise (that sales dropped yesterday) is incorrect if you meant "vs the previous day" — sales rose.  
- Compared with the statistical "usual" for that weekday, net sales were modestly below normal (−12%), and the decomposition shows the shortfall mainly came from lower gross sales and changes in return/discount lines; however the automated causal test found no single upstream cause that meets the evidence threshold. Measured / Insufficient evidence for a cause.
